title: Developing a Deep Learning Model for the Detection of Fibres in the Scanning Electron Microscope
content: The application of machine learning in scientific imaging has been quite appealing for years even though it was initially introduced in 1950s. Machine learning has also been widely applied in cell biology and medicine for prognosis and diagnosis as well as other fields. The research produced is ever-increasing and spans over a multitude of fields (optimisation models, rapid evaluation models, cancer research, communication networks, card games, etc.). Here, we present an application of a deep learning model for the automated detection of fibres in scanning electron microscope images. The motivation for developing this model was driven by the need to quickly screen samples that could potentially contain asbestos and reliably detect, analyse, and confirm the fibres as asbestos or not.
